title: Instrument language must mean moral condition—not physical tool or mere notice
source_text: XXIV. Quin huc tandem necesse est devenire illos ipsos, qui dicunt fidem nos justificare per modum instrumenti, quod apprehendit Christi justitiam, & remissionem peccatorum accipit, si velint mentem suam verbis claris & distinctis, & quae cum veritate & ratione congruunt exponere. Nam, quum dicunt fidem esse instrumentum justificationis, intelligere non possunt instrumentum physicum & proprie dictum. Nec enim fides physice & proprie remissionem peccatorum, in qua justificatio consistit, operatur. Morale vero instrumentum justificationis quomodo potest esse fides, nisi quatenus est conditio quaedam, ad illam ex parte nostra praerequisita? & similiter, quum dicitur fides apprehendere Christi justitiam, propter quam absolvimur in Dei judicio, & remissionem peccatorum oblatam accipere, planum est voces illas acceptionis, & apprehensionis, non esse sumendas proprio, sed metaphorico sensu. Etenim fides non alia de causa dicitur accipere remissionem peccatorum, & apprehendere Christi justitiam, quam quia Deus solis credentibus remissionem peccatorum concedit, & Christi justitiam imputat, ac necesse est in Christum viva fide credere, ut ejus fiamus compotes, & propter Christi meritum & obedientiam acceptemur ad vitam aeternam. Ac plane frigidum esset, & alienum a mente eorum quibuscum agimus, apprehensionem illam exponere de notitia, quam per fidem habemus, de imputata nobis Christi obedientia, remissione peccatorum, merito ejus a Deo impetrata, quia scilicet, dicimur apprehendere quae mente percipimus. Idque jam a nobis satis refutatum est, argumentis iis quibus ostendimus, fidem aliter nos justificare, quam praebendo nobis sensum & notitiam nostrae justificationis.
pass_a_gloss: Indeed those themselves who say faith justifies us by way of an instrument that apprehends Christ's righteousness and receives remission of sins must finally come to this, if they wish to explain their mind in clear and distinct words that agree with truth and reason. For when they say faith is the instrument of justification, they cannot mean a physical instrument properly so called. For faith does not physically and properly effect the remission of sins in which justification consists. But how can faith be a moral instrument of justification except insofar as it is a certain condition prerequisite to it on our part? And likewise, when faith is said to apprehend Christ's righteousness for which we are absolved in God's judgment and to receive the offered remission of sins, it is plain that those words of receiving and apprehending are not to be taken in a proper but a metaphorical sense. For faith is said to receive remission of sins and apprehend Christ's righteousness for no other reason than that God grants remission of sins and imputes Christ's righteousness to believers alone, and it is necessary to believe in Christ with living faith to become partakers of him and be accepted to eternal life for Christ's merit and obedience. And it would be plainly cold and alien to the mind of those with whom we deal to explain that apprehension as the knowledge we have by faith of Christ's obedience imputed to us, of remission of sins, of his merit obtained from God—because, namely, we are said to apprehend what we perceive with the mind. And that has already been sufficiently refuted by us with those arguments by which we showed that faith justifies us otherwise than by giving us the sense and knowledge of our justification.
pass_b_english: Calling faith an 'instrument' cannot mean a physical tool—only a moral prerequisite condition.
'Apprehend/receive' is metaphor for God's granting remission to living believers—not mere notice of prior justification.

choices.why: Metaphor for receiving Christ by living faith.
